- Requirement: The session the pickup starts checks the issue labels, and `/implement-issue-claude` with the `— dispatched` marker checks again and parks the issue when `ai:claude` is gone.
  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md` (the ROOT pickup-side dispatch command) and `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md` (the ROOT pickup-side implementation command).
  Evidence of absence: The PR modifies only the `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/{claude-issue-dispatch,implement-issue-claude}.md` twins. The matching ROOT files in `.claude/commands/` are unchanged: the ROOT `.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md` at line 46 still emits the launch prompt `/implement-issue-claude <url>` (no label precheck, no `— dispatched` marker) and the ROOT `.claude/commands/implement-issue-claude.md` at line 18 still says "Claim — add `ai:claude` if missing and remove `ai:claude-blocked` / `ai:claude-handoff-failed` if present". The pickup session in coding-workflows runs in the coding-workflows checkout and reads from the coding-workflows ROOT (`.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md`), not from the `workflow-templates/.claude/` twin — the twin is the @stable delivery target for consumer repos, not the source the pickup reads. `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` step 3 still reads "Follow `.claude/commands/claude-issue-dispatch.md` **step 2**" and constructs the launch prompt from the unmodified ROOT. The new session started in a consumer repo receives the OLD launch prompt and the OLD implementation command, so the session-side re-check the PR claims to add is rolled out to consumers but is NOT active for sessions started by the coding-workflows pickup. The interim twin-first rule (CLAUDE.md §28.C, until #4785) forbids editing the ROOT `.claude/**` files unattended, so the change is parked in a `hold` claim until a supervising session copies the twins — but the PR description and the changelog fragment claim the safety holds today, which is true only for consumer repos whose `@stable` sync has copied both twins, and false for sessions the coding-workflows pickup starts into a consumer that has not synced the new twins. (The same finding was raised by openai_gpt-6-luna at confidence 5 in the cross-pollination summary.)
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
